senses.gloss: (b. h., √<cite ref="Q01221"><he>פס</he></cite> , v. <he>פסס</he> to cut off)

to be gone.—[As a noun: there is an end of …] B. Bath. 111ᵃ אפס (דברי) זכריה (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l.) (the words of) Zachariah (to whom you refer as an authority) are (is) gone, i.e. they are no authority.

homiletically used as though a Greek word (ἄφες) let go, leave alone. Pesik. Vattomer p. 130ᵃ (ref. to heäfes, Ps. LXXVII, 9) לשון יוני הוא כמד״א אָפֵיס it is a Greek word, as if you were to say, afes (let alone); Lam. R. to I, 2 וכמד״א אמר אפס (strike out ואמר, a. read אפיס); Ex. R. s. 45 לשון יוני אפס הניח in Greek aphes means, (he) let go; Yalk. Ps. 816.—[Gen. R. s. 40 (ref. to efes Jud. IV, 9); omitted in Yalk. Gen. 67,—an interpolation from passages quoted above.]
